issues.description: IAM getIamPolicy failure silently yields publicly_shared=False, so PASS no longer means 'verified non-public'.
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied on fixture image 3), the except branch logs and falls through, appending the image with publicly_shared=False. The check then reports PASS for an image whose policy was never read. Introduce an explicit unknown/MANUAL state or surface an error finding so an auth failure does not look like a clean bill of health.

issues.description: PR description name (compute_image_publicly_shared) disagrees with shipped paths/CheckID (compute_image_not_publicly_shared).
issues.detail: The metadata, directory, class, and CHANGELOG use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, while the PR body repeatedly says compute_image_publicly_shared. The check name is the contract identifier callers and dashboards bind to. Pick one and propagate everywhere before merge.

issues.description: Image listing does not filter custom vs public/marketplace/deprecated images despite spec claim.
issues.detail: images().list(project=project_id) is called with no filter (e.g., deprecated.state, family, source), yet the PR claims the check evaluates only 'custom images'. If that is the precondition, enforce it in code; otherwise update the spec. As written the check may spam findings on images outside its stated scope.

issues.description: Image ADT is too thin — stores only a derived boolean and lacks self_link/location context.
issues.detail: The Image model carries publicly_shared but drops the bindings (roles, members) that justify it and omits self_link/region fields present on sibling ADTs. Remediation, audit logs, and findings across multi-project/family namespaces need that context. Storing public_members and a resource URI keeps the abstraction self-describing and matches the file's conventions.

issues.description: Service test pins leaky behavior: asserts publicly_shared=False for the IAM-policy exception case.
issues.detail: test-image-3 raises in getIamPolicy and the test asserts publicly_shared is False, conflating 'truly not shared' with 'policy fetch failed'. The most security-relevant failure mode is never exercised at the check layer, and the assertion will make the correct fix (unknown/MANUAL) a test-breaking change.

issues.description: Image listing is serial while every other resource in compute_service.py uses __threading_call__.
issues.detail: _get_images iterates project_ids serially in the constructor, breaking the file's established pattern of parallelizing collection over projects/regions/zones. Either match the surrounding style or state a specific reason. The inconsistency is a maintenance trap and a perf regression for accounts with many projects.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, single-purpose check that is NEEDS-WORK rather than ready to ship. The dominant defect is a contract violation on the failure path: when getIamPolicy raises, the image is recorded with publicly_shared=False and the check reports PASS, so an auth failure looks like a clean image — and the tests pin that behavior. Naming is inconsistent between the PR description and the shipped artifacts, and the image listing lacks the filter its spec implies. The Image ADT is thinner than sibling models, and the collection loop ignores the file's established __threading_call__ pattern. Fix the unknown-policy postcondition, reconcile the name, and the rest is acceptable.
